stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model licensed under Apache 2.0, targeting local coding agents.
The model is optimized for local deployment via Ollama, featuring new native DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Moderna and Merck say their mRNA cancer vaccine cut death, recurrence by 42%
stories.author: Beth Mole
bullet_points: Moderna and Merck reported top-line results for their mRNA cancer vaccine.
The vaccine demonstrated a significant reduction in cancer death and recurrence by 42%.
This represents a major advancement in cancer immunotherapy using mRNA technology.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text-generation and conversational tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in large language model tasks.
The tags confirm its relevance within the transformer and Llama ecosystem.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function as a large language model.
The associated tags (transformers, safetensors, llama) confirm its relevance within the modern NLP/AI ecosystem.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically engineered for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is designed to run efficiently on local, personal hardware.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent tasks show up to 90% faster performance based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Feds want robotaxis to signal ‘I’m driving’ with cyan-colored lights
stories.author: Andrew J. Hawkins
bullet_points: The NHTSA has mandated a specific visual signal for autonomous vehicles.
The required signal is cyan-colored lights to indicate that the vehicle is operating without a human driver.
This decision resolves a long-standing debate among stakeholders regarding how robotaxis should communicate their autonomous status.

stories.title: SpaceX’s mobile carrier push reportedly involves tapping into 80,000 cell sites
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: SpaceX is aggressively moving into the mobile carrier market to challenge incumbents like Verizon and T-Mobile.
The strategy involves securing access to a massive network of at least 80,000 existing cell sites.
SpaceX is reportedly in discussions with Crown Castle Inc., a major tower infrastructure owner.

stories.title: Meta delays new business terms after publisher pushback on AI scraping
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Meta is delaying the rollout of new business terms due to publisher objections.
The core concern from publishers is that the terms could permit Meta to scrape news sites for AI training data.
The enforcement date for the terms has been pushed back, with a new target date of November 20th.

stories.title: Ukraine learns to fight without Starlink as Musk plays politics with satellites
stories.author: Jeremy Hsu
bullet_points: Ukraine is actively diversifying its military technology to decrease dependence on Starlink.
The shift indicates a strategic move to mitigate geopolitical risks associated with reliance on private satellite infrastructure.
The story highlights the intersection of military necessity, technological adaptation, and corporate/political influence (Musk's role).

stories.title: Disgraced eMudhra drops out of TLS business after using cert private key of 4
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: eMudhra, a digital certificate authority, has exited the TLS business following a major security failure.
The vulnerability stemmed from a flawed key signing process, allowing unauthorized issuance of web credentials.
The flaw potentially enabled the minting of valid web credentials for any website.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents' safety and evidence recovery.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents can execute prohibited actions if tool responses omit safety-relevant facts.
The benchmark includes 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six different domains for rigorous evaluation.

stories.title: VERA: A Responsible AI Dashboard for Assessing LLM Deployments in Light of the EU AI Act
stories.author: Jérôme Lebecq
bullet_points: VERA is a new dashboard designed to help institutions demonstrate responsible AI practices when deploying LLMs.
It provides a technical interpretation of the EU AI Act, organizing required evidence into six principle groups and eighteen technical requirements.
The system aims to bridge the gap between technical measurement (via command-line benchmarks) and non-technical regulatory approval.

stories.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
stories.author: Shuang Qiu
bullet_points: Introduces EpiSEM-Bench, a new benchmark designed to test LLM agents' safety when environmental facts are missing from tool responses.
Addresses a critical vulnerability where agents might perform prohibited actions even with benign user requests if safety-relevant facts are omitted.
The benchmark includes 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains to evaluate unsafe execution and evidence recovery.

stories.title: Would an LLM Match into a Residency? Uncertainty, Reasoning and Image Use of Open Language Models on the Spanish MIR Examination
stories.author: Aitor Almeida
bullet_points: The research investigates the limitations of open LLMs when applied to high-stakes medical exams (Spanish MIR).
Key focus areas include assessing the models' uncertainty, reasoning soundness, and actual utilization of provided medical images.
The study evaluates four open language models (8-27B parameters) to inform the safe deployment of AI in healthcare systems.

stories.title: The Geometry of Metaphor: Probing and Steering Metaphor Representations in Large Language Models
stories.author: Martha Lewis
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) internally represent the complex cognitive concept of metaphor.
It employs mechanistic interpretability to find causal subspaces within various LLM architectures and sizes.
The study demonstrates the ability to steer LLM outputs, both in classification and generation tasks, based on metaphor representations.

stories.title: Agents should never hold your API keys. NVIDIA just open-sourced the runtime that enforces it
stories.author: slabb
bullet_points: NVIDIA has open-sourced OpenShell, a new runtime designed to enhance security for AI agent fleets.
OpenShell enforces strict security by providing kernel-level sandboxes to agents, preventing them from storing API keys.
The system incorporates a Z3 SMT prover to validate policy changes before human approval, adding a layer of automated governance.

stories.title: Clef is available on Ollama's cloud
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Cloudflare's 27B multimodal decision model, Clef, is now integrated with Ollama.
Users have the option to run the Clef model either locally or via Ollama's cloud service.
This expands the accessibility of advanced, large-scale multimodal AI models within the Ollama ecosystem.

stories.title: Reflection's Beam is freely available on Ollama for a limited time
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Reflection's open-weight model, Beam, is now available on Ollama.
Beam is specifically designed for software engineering, reasoning, and agentic tasks.
The model is offered free for a limited time via Ollama Cloud.

stories.title: Run AI agents safely with Ollama and Fly.io
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama enables the safe execution of AI agents.
The integration allows these agents to run within Fly.io's cloud infrastructure.
This combination addresses the need for secure deployment of local/cloud AI models.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama now integrates support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These new models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
Decision models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to leverage open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Retro gaming is being overrun with AI
stories.author: Andrew Webster
bullet_points: AI tools are driving a surge in unexpected and viral retro gaming projects.
Examples include porting classic games like Halo to web browsers and Wind Waker to mobile.
This trend highlights the accessibility and creative application of current AI technologies in entertainment.

stories.title: Switch 2 security takes a hit as hackers unlock homebrew access
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Security vulnerability discovered in the upcoming Switch 2.
The exploit, a 'userland' vulnerability, utilizes an integer overflow in the SmileBasic interpreter.
Hackers have successfully gained homebrew access to the system.

stories.title: Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization for Thought Pruning: Balancing Quality and Diversity in Test-Time Reasoning
stories.author: Meisam Razaviyayn
bullet_points: The paper addresses the computational cost of test-time scaling in reasoning models, where many candidate solutions are generated.
It introduces 'Direct Pass@$k$ Optimization' as a method to intelligently prune candidate solutions after generating only a short prefix.
The core focus is balancing the quality (finding correct answers) and diversity of the remaining candidates during inference.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: METTA introduces a novel approach for Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation in Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
It addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories needed for rapid adaptation in RL agents.
The method aims to overcome the quadratic memory and computation costs associated with traditional transformer-based trajectory retrieval.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high memory consumption of n-gram embedding tables used in modern open-weight language models.
These embedding tables store learned representations of short token sequences (n-grams) to boost model performance.
The research aims to reduce the memory footprint of these n-gram embeddings while maintaining or improving model performance.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a core limitation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final prediction.
Introduces 'CausalCoT,' a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency in large language model reasoning.
The method mitigates 'attention leakage' by isolating context during the step-by-step generation process.

stories.title: Sensorimotor Alignment: A Platonic Proxy for Embodied Policy Success
stories.author: Chen Wei
bullet_points: The paper proposes using cheap offline proxies to evaluate robotic foundation models, moving away from expensive closed-loop rollouts.

It introduces the Platonic Representation Hypothesis (PRH), suggesting that different modalities (vision, language, motion) should converge into a shared statistical model of reality as models improve.
The core research question investigates whether motion trajectories can serve as another modality in this convergence toward a unified representation.

stories.title: Phase Transition from Random Features to Fully Trainable Networks
stories.author: Shijun Zhang
bullet_points: The research explores a 'phase transition' phenomenon when moving from fixed random features to fully trainable neural networks.
Partially trainable neural networks are introduced as a bridge between fixed and adaptive representation learning.
The study quantifies this transition using approximation bounds and observes similar behavior in training error curves.

stories.title: SpectralCanary: Embarrassingly Simple Low-Frequency Traces for T2I Dataset-Use Auditing
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: SpectralCanary introduces a novel method for auditing if Text-to-Image (T2I) models were fine-tuned on specific datasets.
The technique works by embedding a 'shared signal' (a low-frequency trace) into a dataset before release and checking for its presence in model outputs.
It addresses the challenge where models can absorb dataset characteristics without reproducing original training images, improving upon existing trade-offs in auditing.

stories.title: METTA: Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation for Meta-Reinforcement Learning
stories.author: Mahdieh Soleymani Baghshah
bullet_points: METTA proposes a new Memory-Enhanced Test-Time Adaptation technique for Meta-Reinforcement Learning.
It addresses the challenge of representing long interaction histories required for fast adaptation in meta-RL agents.
The method aims to overcome the quadratic memory and computational costs associated with traditional transformer-based trajectory retrieval.

stories.title: Causal Chain of Thought: Mitigating Attention Leakage via Context Isolation
stories.author: Martin Gjoreski
bullet_points: Addresses a fundamental limitation of Chain-of-Thought (CoT) prompting: the generated reasoning steps may not causally drive the final prediction.
Introduces CausalCoT, a new inference framework designed to enforce causal transparency during model reasoning.
Aims to mitigate 'attention leakage' in standard autoregressive models where dense attention allows for plausible but ungrounded justifications.

stories.title: BeNice! Closing Looping's Inference-Memory Gap via KV-Sharing
stories.author: Daniel Y. Fu
bullet_points: The paper addresses the memory bottleneck in looped neural network architectures, where repeated inference generates independent KV-caches.
The core problem is the linear memory growth during inference caused by these independent KV-caches in recurrent setups.
The proposed solution, 'BeNice!', leverages KV-sharing (KV-s) to reuse KV-caches across different recurrence depths without sacrificing model quality.

stories.title: Low-Bit N-Gram Embeddings for Language Models
stories.author: Wenyu Du
bullet_points: The paper addresses the high memory consumption associated with n-gram embedding tables in modern language models.
These embedding tables, used by models like DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, store learned representations of short token sequences (n-grams).
The research aims to reduce the memory footprint of these n-gram embeddings while maintaining model performance.

stories.title: Can an Agent Debug a Web Corpus? Agentic Auditing of Slovak FineWeb2
stories.author: Jaroslav Kopčan
bullet_points: Proposes using an LLM as a 'corpus debugger' to find unforeseen failure modes in large multilingual datasets like FineWeb2.
The agent interacts with the corpus via a read-only, budgeted API, generating executable tests for human validation.
Demonstrated effectiveness on the Slovak portion of FineWeb2, identifying seven issues across multiple runs.

stories.title: Diffusion Language Models for Perplexity-Aware Black-Box Attacks
stories.author: Suhang Wang
bullet_points: The research introduces diffusion language models for generating perplexity-aware black-box attacks against LLMs.
These attacks operate in a continuous-space latent Gaussian space, decoding to text via a random mapping and nearest-token lookup.
A key limitation noted is that the resulting prompts are often unnatural due to the random mapping, potentially making them detectable by guardrails.

stories.title: An Empirical Study of Recent Large Language Models for Knowledge Graph to Text Generation on Standard Benchmarks
stories.author: Antoine Doucet
bullet_points: The study empirically benchmarks recent Large Language Models (LLMs) for Knowledge Graph-to-Text (KG-to-text) generation.
It compares LLMs against traditional fine-tuned encoder-decoder models using standard and graph-grounded evaluation metrics.
The findings indicate that recent LLMs are significantly narrowing the performance gap with established methods in this generation task.

stories.title: Show HN: We had AI write a wiki from 45k Enron emails, every fact cited
stories.author: jreynar
bullet_points: Demonstration of AI's capability to synthesize large, unstructured datasets (45k emails).
The system successfully generated a wiki structure from the raw email data.
A key feature highlighted is the citation of every fact, indicating a focus on verifiability.

stories.title: AI Is Winning Literary Awards. The Data Says That's Not What's Happening.
stories.author: james_anderson_h
bullet_points: The article addresses the growing media narrative surrounding AI winning literary awards.
It challenges the prevailing narrative by suggesting the data does not support the idea that AI is dominating literary recognition.
The discussion centers on the intersection of generative AI and creative fields like literature.
